text: Heap explainer (concepts/heap/heap-explorer.html) is unreadable: nodes and array cells are solid black with black text, through the app and from disk. The file is a fragment that expects a host page's colour variables (--foreground, --muted) and has no doctype, title or viewport. Seen in the browser test run of 2026-11-16.

Arrays & Hashing explainer opens at section 3, not the top: the doubling prediction gate focuses its first button when it renders on load (box.querySelector('button').focus(), about line 400). Same through the app and from disk.

Explainers are served sandboxed by the app, so localStorage throws; references/explainers.md doesn't say so, and tests/browser/check_app.py uses a placeholder explainer, so it passed while the Arrays & Hashing stepper was dead. That page was fixed in 78b3214 (blocked a session); the guide and the check are unchanged.

Improve it: feedback typed into 'What should change?' is wiped when the tab regains focus, because the visibilitychange reload redraws the Learn page (it only skips while the handoff is open). The hint under the box tells him to attempt a problem first, which is what triggers it.
The 'Ask your coach' handoff panel stays open across views: it followed to Today, covered half the Due list with a stale prompt, and while it is open the page doesn't reload itself on return.

Today shows a stale live solve as current: 'block 10: 15 of 15 min' for contains-duplicate, untouched for 6 days, with no age and no prompt to resume, park or drop it. The session-start hook says all three; the page has last_active and doesn't use it.
Today's Due list is 17 equal rows: it doesn't mark the three for today (REVIEWS_PER_DAY), shows slugs where the Learn page shows titles, and repeats contains-duplicate, which is also the live solve.

Scroll isn't reset between views. At side-panel width, opening a pattern from low on the one-column map lands with the title and explainer button above the viewport, and '← Map' returns to the top of the map. Likewise the server-offline notice is out of view if he presses Refresh while scrolled, so nothing seems to happen.

Smaller things from the browser test run: the panel hides the 'Next re-solve' column but keeps Status; the map says 'Blind 75 1/8' for Arrays & Hashing beside eight rows marked 'last: solved'; quotes in Improve-it feedback appear escaped in the prompt (JSON.stringify); the tab title is 'DSA Coach' on every view; Cmd+Enter doesn't submit the feedback form.
Binary Search explainer focuses too narrowly on target lookup in a sorted array. Broaden where binary search applies and how to recognize the pattern; requested revision logged as q0006.

Asked whether the coach should be an MCP server instead of, or alongside, the Chrome extension. Discussed 2026-11-17: the panel is a view for him beside LeetCode and an MCP server can't replace it. A local MCP server adds nothing where coach.py already runs (Claude Code, Codex). A remote one would replace the web-chat export/delta round trip (ARCHITECTURE.md step 5), but no web session has happened yet. Revisit if he studies away from the Mac, or with the testers/course layer.

Continues f0011 (same conversation; count the two as one note at triage). His idea: an MCP server that holds everything known about what works for his learning, so he can chat with Claude directly, outside this workspace, and it knows how he learns. Discussed 2026-11-17: techniques.json is still empty; docs/research names a memory profile in every chat as the largest sycophancy risk; a chat with the profile but without the skill's rules isn't the coach. The shape to revisit is skill + MCP together (ARCHITECTURE.md step 5), once the ledger has rows that aren't provisional and he studies in the Claude app.

Generate the explainer for each topic now, ahead of time, and focus on in-depth understanding of patterns. Same theme as f0010 (the Binary Search page was too narrow: where the pattern applies and how to spot it). Two parts: (1) every pattern has its explainer ready before he reaches it; today 5 of 22 patterns have one, and learn mode builds a pattern's explainer when he starts it; (2) explainers teach the pattern in depth, not one problem. The Binary Search v2 of 2026-11-16 (recognition questions, monotone predicates, transfer checks) is the closest example of the depth he means.
Expected to type stage answers/inputs in the Chrome side panel during a solve; it has no input box (search-in-rotated-sorted-array, stage 1)

Drop the stage 1 restatement step; it feels like retyping the problem. (Context: on search-in-rotated-sorted-array the restatement surfaced that he had LC 153's goal - return the minimum - in mind, and missed the distinct-values property.)
Skip predicting outputs in stage 1; the problem's own examples already show them. (Coach kept only the edge case that isn't on the page: rotated n times.)
Start every solve at stage 2 (Find an approach); see f0015.
Stage 4 asks too much writing (why it works, lesson, extra question). Wants the coach to give pointers and the answers when he says he knows.

Likes the INDEX 0 desktop app (index-0.in) for learning DSA, system design and more; asked whether the coach should do something like it, or expose an MCP server. Found 2026-11-21: INDEX 0 (v1.9.2, free, closed source, local-first) has 475 DSA problems in six stages with solutions withheld until the end, an in-app judged editor, roadmaps (system design 102 lessons, ML, electronics, security), quiz mode, mock interviews with a report, and an AI coach on local Ollama/Gemma or a BYO key that keeps notes about the user. Its pages state no spaced repetition and no MCP. Coach's take: the gap it shows is a system design course (ARCHITECTURE.md 2c), which the 90-day plan doesn't include; its editor, games and badges are PRODUCT.md anti-references. The MCP part repeats f0011/f0012 (count them together at triage); the trigger to revisit is studying from the Claude app away from the Mac.
